properties.name: The records a choice actually rests on carry a truth, a counter-argument is its own statement, and a settled decision shows its acceptance and its chain side by side
properties.source: @ajs, 2026-10-18, choosing A of the build list after the embedding proof of concept
properties.statement:
From the 2026-10-18 proof of concept (fact:reasoning-embedded-in-a-traditional-design-works-within-one-design-and-stops-at-premises-with-no-truth-and-at-design-borders-2026-10-18, case 1):
1. A measured, unsuperseded finding (TemporalFact) used as a premise reads `holds`; superseded or invalidated, it does not.
2. A counter-argument is recorded as a statement of its own that opposes the claim, so answering it never marks a historical record (a ChangeEvent) false.
3. An accepted Decision concluded by a chain reads the owner's acceptance AND the chain's verdict side by side, so a first, incomplete chain never reads as the decision being unsupported. Its read-back shows `chose`, not the deliberation's "options, none chosen".
4. The served skills agree on whether an Inference may conclude a Decision (capture-intent vs brainstorm/AGENTS.md).
